title: Inca Empire
capsule: The Inca Empire (Quechua: Tawantinsuyu, 'Realm of the Four Parts') was the largest polity in pre-Columbian America, centered at Cusco and extending some 4,000 kilometers along the Andes from modern southern Colombia to central Chile. Under Pachacuti (r. 1438–1471) and his son Tupac Inca Yupanqui (r. 1471–1493) the empire expanded rapidly through conquest and alliance, organizing its territories through a road network exceeding 40,000 kilometers, mit'a labor service, and the quipu recording system. Francisco Pizarro's expedition of 168 men captured the emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca on 16 November 1532, and the execution of Atahualpa in 1533 broke centralized resistance; the last independent Inca ruler, Tupac Amaru I, was captured and beheaded by the Spanish viceroy Toledo in 1572.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is well attested by Spanish colonial administrative records, road surveys (qhapaq ñan), and modern archaeology; the Andean core is high-confidence while the eastern Amazonian fringe and southern limits are approximate, reconstructed from provincial administrative lists (Suyus).
